head_commit.message:
Record the console at 1920x1080, with its own frame masters

Every media artifact in this repository misses the geometry it declares. The two
terminal GIFs are 2049x1323 and 1903x1228, the second of those despite being
named "1080", and the Portal capture is 1920x1200. The bullet.real-media.v1
manifest declares 1920x1080 and nothing has ever produced it.

The arithmetic was never hard, it was simply never done. Tuiwright renders a
screen as cols*cell_width by rows*cell_height and draws real JetBrains Mono
scaled to the cell height, so a larger cell means larger glyphs rather than gaps.
120 columns by 36 rows at a 16x30 cell with no padding is exactly 1920x1080, and
120x36 is a terminal size a person would actually use.

Run against the live console on this host, just now:

    DEVNODE_RECORD_COMPLETE: tui-1080p.gif at 1920x1080, 9 frames, 9 masters

Frames come from the pseudo-terminal own parsed screen model, so they are native
frames rather than a re-render of an asciicast. Every frame is also written as a
lossless 1920x1080 PNG, because the M1 gate asks for original masters and
media/dogfood/README.md states plainly that the current packet has none. The
recorder reads the geometry back out of the encoded file own header and refuses
DEVNODE_RECORD_GIF_GEOMETRY_DRIFT rather than trusting the encoder, which is the
check every existing artifact would have failed.

Two properties worth naming because they are the reason to trust the output. It
records nothing it has not first asserted, so the artifact cannot contain a frame
the harness did not verify. And run.json names the beats it did NOT record and
why: today that is every beat needing durable work, because the ledger holds
none, and inventing rows would make the recording a mock.

The lane builds it and does not run it. A recording is a deliberate act against a
real session with a private output directory; a lane that published media as a
side effect would be publishing without anyone asking.

The proof-only manifest class now holds two entries, which is what it was built
for. Product manifest pins and the seven subject pins remain byte-identical to
main, and the canary covers the second harness exactly as it covers the first.

head_commit.message:
Give the harness its own workspace root, or it cannot build at all

Found by running the lane against the live authenticated daemon rather than by
reading it. devnode/tui/Cargo.toml said it was "excluded from the Hub workspace"
and nothing excluded it, so cargo read ../../Cargo.toml and refused:

    error: current package believes it is in a workspace when it is not
    current:   devnode/tui/Cargo.toml
    workspace: Cargo.toml

An empty [workspace] table in the harness manifest makes it its own root. Doing
it there rather than through an `exclude` in the Hub manifest keeps every product
manifest byte-identical, which is the promise the proof-only class rests on. The
proof-only pin is regenerated for the new bytes.

This is exactly the failure the hosted graph cannot catch, because the lane
refuses to run hosted by design. It was caught the only way it could be: by
running the lane. All eight console flows then pass against a real authenticated
session on this host, serially, in 7.31 seconds.

head_commit.message:
Make the scheduled lanes able to run at all

All four scheduled workflows had never executed once. Their crons fire on
Mondays and the repositories were created on a Wednesday, and workflow_dispatch
was enabled the whole time, so twenty-six of fifty-three job definitions had
simply never been observed. I dispatched three of them. Eleven jobs failed. Four
of the five hub failures are fixed here, each with its cause named.

Windows could not check the repository out. Not the lane: the checkout.

    error: invalid path 'fixtures/hostile/cases/nul.json'
    ##[error]The process 'git.exe' failed with exit code 128

`nul` is a reserved device name on Windows, so git cannot create that file and
every Windows claim this repository has ever made is about a checkout that never
happened. The fixture is renamed to nul-character.json, which is what it was
always about: a NUL character inside JSON, not a filename. Same bytes, same
CONTROL_CHARACTER_FORBIDDEN reason code, generator and consumer both updated.

macOS could not install Python. setup-python refused with "The version '3.12.12'
with architecture 'arm64' was not found for macOS 15.7.9". The exact patch was
never load-bearing: ops/ci/rust-toolchain-boundary.sh accepts any
^Python 3\.12\.[0-9]+$ and then verifies the resolved binary by digest. The pin
is now the 3.12 series, in the workflow and in the guard that asserts it, which
still stops a silent jump to 3.13 — the thing that guard is actually for.

Coverage never had a scanner. The coverage filter is the whole workspace, wider
than the fast lane's partition, so it reaches
publication::scan::tests::actual_pinned_scanner_detects_binary_and_chunk_boundary_canaries,
which admits the pinned scanner rather than skipping and therefore panicked at
src/publication/scan_tests.rs:130. The fast job already installs gitleaks for

head_commit.message:
Render the repair metadata CoordError has always carried

Every CoordError in this crate carries four facts beyond its code and reason:
the purpose of the boundary that refused, at least two concrete fixes, a narrow
next step, and a repository-relative documentation anchor. repair_metadata fills
all four for every code, the anchors all resolve in docs/errors.md, and there is
a test asserting there are never fewer than two fixes.

None of it has ever reached an operator. Display writes "{code}: {reason}" and
nothing read the rest, so the only consumers of purpose, common_fixes, docs_url
and repair_hint were four assertions in the test suite. A person running the CLI
saw a bare token like UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA and had to read the source to find out
what to do about it. Now they see this:

    bullet-family: UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA
      family.lock schema 2 is not installable; retain it for diagnosis, regenerate schema 3 from authenticated signed tags, and replace it atomically

      protecting    reject a schema outside the admitted version set
      try           - follow the explicit export or removal procedure
                    - use the binary and lock version that own the subject
      next          follow the schema-removal or setup-recovery runbook
      docs          docs/errors.md#unsupported-or-corrupt-state

Display is untouched and always will be: it is the machine contract, a great
deal of tooling greps stderr for "CODE: reason", and the rendered form still
leads with the code on line one so those greps keep working. For the same reason
the reason text is never hard-wrapped. Wrapping it broke
release_profiles::ordinary_release_requires_an_explicit_profile, which greps for
a phrase that a newline had landed in the middle of. That failure was the useful
kind: it says exactly which text is a surface other people depend on. A terminal
soft-wraps a long line by itself at no cost, so only the metadata block, which
nothing greps because until now it was never printed, is laid out to a width.

One colour rule, in one place, with no new dependency. src/diagnostic.rs decides
once, from values passed in rather than looked up, so the rule is a pure function
with tests: NO_COLOR when present and non-empty, CLICOLOR_FORCE to paint a pipe,
a dumb or absent TERM never painted even when forced, and otherwise the depth the
terminal advertises. Three tiers, because a palette that emits truecolor
unconditionally is a bet rather than a palette. --no-color, --plain and
--color=<auto|always|never> are new and are stripped from argv before dispatch,
since colour is a property of the terminal and not of any command.

The 985-character single-line USAGE is now a grouped listing. Nothing asserted on
its exact text; tests/family_lock.rs asserted on one concatenated fragment of it,
and that assertion is now two assertions plus a negative one, which is stricter
than what it replaced: it would catch one verb's arguments drifting while the
other's did not.

Test inventory: hub 600 to 616, total 819 to 835, both identity digests
regenerated by running ops/ci/test-partitions.sh rather than by editing numbers.

head_commit.message:
Register the devnode lane in the proof-lane registry

The hosted fast lane caught what my local lint lane could not: assurance_controls
control_manifests_route_to_real_local_proof parses every non-empty line between
`case "$lane" in` and `*)` in scripts/ci-local.sh as a dispatcher row, so the two
comment lines I put beside the new case arm were read as malformed rows. The note
now sits above the case statement, where it is still next to the thing it
explains and is not mistaken for a row.

With that fixed the same test reported the real omission: a new lane must be
declared in agent/proof-lanes.toml and in the expected registry, or the
dispatcher and the registry disagree. Both now carry devnode, with
requires_network true, because the lane fetches the pinned Tuiwright revision and
talks to a daemon.

That test is the control that stops a lane from existing in the dispatcher while
being invisible to the register, which is a near relative of the finding this
whole branch closes.

head_commit.message:
Publish the dev-node lane at canonical paths and pin its harness

operator_review reported four times that it could not find devnode/tui or
ops/ci/devnode.sh anywhere in the repository. It was right: the lane existed
only in a scratch tree on the development host, so nobody could review the
thing I was citing as proof. This puts every byte of it at a canonical path.

The lane drives `bullet tui` through a real pseudo-terminal and the Portal
through a real browser, both against an authenticated daemon. That session and
the provider credentials behind it exist on one machine, so the lane refuses to
run anywhere else, twice over: ops/ci/devnode.sh refuses under GITHUB_ACTIONS,
and ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh refuses any hosted workflow that so much as names
it. The second guard is the one a maintainer trips over first, so it is the one
with hostile fixtures: a job that runs the lane, a commented-out mention, a
matrix entry, and a symlinked workflow entry.

Manifest classification, per the review. My first attempt pruned ./devnode from
the build-subject search. Both reviewers rejected that and they were right:
pruning would have made every future manifest under that directory invisible to
the guard, which is the opposite of what the guard is for. Instead there are now
two pinned classes. Product manifests are what ships. Proof manifests belong to
harnesses that are never a product dependency and are built by no lane other
than the one they prove; crates/bullet-wire/fuzz/Cargo.toml set that precedent
and devnode/tui/Cargo.toml joins it. Both the manifest and its lock are
digest-pinned exactly as a product manifest is, and four new canary cases cover
what pruning would have let through: a second harness beside the pinned one, a
missing harness, a changed harness dependency, and a changed lock.

The four product manifest pins and the seven existing subject pins are
byte-identical to main.

Proved on the development host before pushing: the lint lane passes end to end,
the build-subject canary passes and fails on a falsified pin, and the workflow
policy passes and fails when the devnode guard is neutered.

head_commit.message:
Gate real recordings on their own evidence, and record why 1920x1080 needs lossless padding

scripts/readme-check.sh validates the two synthetic drawtext GIFs the hub README
embeds: exactly 1200x675, 12 fps, under 3 MiB, and byte-identical on re-render.
A real capture cannot satisfy any of that, so a recording of an actual run had
no gate at all. These two scripts give it one.

scripts/readme-real-check.sh accepts a recording only against its own manifest:
1920x1080, under 50,000,000 bytes, monotonic frame delays, the recorder and
render-tool digests, the exact binaries and all four member commits, the run and
receipt identity, the provider and its enrolled runtime version, a redacted
account label, and a retained pre-quantisation master. Claims come from a fixed
allowlist that cannot contain TRANSACTION_PROOF, independent, LIVE_PROOF,
release or self-hosted-v1, and the cast is scanned for bootstrap tokens, CSRF
tokens, undeclared 64-hex values, emails and home paths. Its --self-test proves
two acceptances and 38 typed refusals.

scripts/media/record-tui.sh replaces the ad-hoc media/dogfood wrappers: explicit
run and proof directories rather than "the latest one", the narration's exit
status propagated, the capture retained on failure, and the gate run at the end.

The geometry is worth recording. The tracked renderer calls agg without a font
size, and agg's layout is width = round((cols+2) * font_size * 0.602051),
height = round((rows+1) * font_size * line_height). At line height 1.4 no
integer pair reaches height 1080, and width 1920 would need (cols+2)*font_size
to equal 3 x 1063, which no grid under 240 columns provides. Exactly 1920x1080
is therefore unreachable from a native agg render, which is why the retained
recording is 2049x1323. The recorder renders the largest fitting grid
(225x54 -> 1913x1078) and centres it by rewriting only the logical screen size,
the background index, the global table's entry 0 and each frame offset; the gate
re-derives the canvas from the GIF's own image descriptors and refuses unless
every frame carries a local colour table. Losslessness is proven by cropping the
padded GIF back and comparing framemd5 and the pts sequence.

Proof: `readme-real-check.sh --self-test` exit 0 (2 accepted, 38 refusals);
`record-tui.sh --self-test` exit 0, ending in a PASS at 1920x1080; shellcheck -x
exit 0 for both; the existing real recording is correctly refused
REAL_MEDIA_GEOMETRY: 2049x1323; a narration exiting 7 propagates 7 and retains
its capture.

head_commit.message:
Add the operator scripts that bring a dogfood control plane up, bind a harness, and drive the worker

Starting a dogfood session meant re-deriving a peer registry, a lease transport
key, a bootstrap exchange, a binary manifest and twenty-five BULLET_HARNESS_*
values by hand from a CI proof script. These five scripts do that, refuse by
name when an input is absent, and never print a token, cookie or CSRF value.

- scripts/dogfood/serve.sh admits the data directory, provisions the lease
  transport key create-once, writes the peer registry, launches farmd, waits for
  /health, exchanges the one-time bootstrap and writes a 0600 session file. It
  detects `--bootstrap-token-file` and falls back to scraping the startup line,
  because the current daemon offers neither flag yet.
- scripts/dogfood/prepare-harness.sh derives the harness environment for
  --provider claude, writes a 0600 env file and gates on `bullet coding
  harness-check` reporting BOUND. Three names have no producer anywhere in the
  kernel today, so they are emitted as PLACEHOLDER_DRY_RUN_ONLY, named in the
  script's own output, and refused unless --allow-placeholders is given.
- scripts/dogfood/worker-loop.sh builds the command-worker binary manifest and
  supervises the one-shot worker, logging each COMMAND_UNKNOWN / NO_COMMAND
  result and never restarting a child mid-flight.
- scripts/stage-rust-toolchain.sh prepares, but never installs, an immutable
  root-owned Rust toolchain for a future real gate, and prints the exact
  privileged commands for the operator.
- scripts/dogfood/README.md carries the flow, every refusal code, and what these
  scripts do not prove.

Proof, no provider spawned and nothing spent: shellcheck -x and --help exit 0
for all four scripts; a smoke lane brought farmd up, admitted one run_demo
command (HTTP 202), ran the worker against it, and stopped cleanly; a second
lane proved the idle path exits on NO_COMMAND; prepare-harness reported BOUND
with all eight dogfood names present, and refused
DOGFOOD_OPS_HARNESS_PLACEHOLDERS_PRESENT without the explicit flag.

head_commit.message:
Add the operator scripts that bring a dogfood control plane up, bind a harness, and drive the worker

Starting a dogfood session meant re-deriving a peer registry, a lease transport
key, a bootstrap exchange, a binary manifest and twenty-five BULLET_HARNESS_*
values by hand from a CI proof script. These five scripts do that, refuse by
name when an input is absent, and never print a token, cookie or CSRF value.

- scripts/dogfood/serve.sh admits the data directory, provisions the lease
  transport key create-once, writes the peer registry, launches farmd, waits for
  /health, exchanges the one-time bootstrap and writes a 0600 session file. It
  detects `--bootstrap-token-file` and falls back to scraping the startup line,
  because the current daemon offers neither flag yet.
- scripts/dogfood/prepare-harness.sh derives the harness environment for
  --provider claude, writes a 0600 env file and gates on `bullet coding
  harness-check` reporting BOUND. Three names have no producer anywhere in the
  kernel today, so they are emitted as PLACEHOLDER_DRY_RUN_ONLY, named in the
  script's own output, and refused unless --allow-placeholders is given.
- scripts/dogfood/worker-loop.sh builds the command-worker binary manifest and
  supervises the one-shot worker, logging each COMMAND_UNKNOWN / NO_COMMAND
  result and never restarting a child mid-flight.
- scripts/stage-rust-toolchain.sh prepares, but never installs, an immutable
  root-owned Rust toolchain for a future real gate, and prints the exact
  privileged commands for the operator.
- scripts/dogfood/README.md carries the flow, every refusal code, and what these
  scripts do not prove.

Proof, no provider spawned and nothing spent: shellcheck -x and --help exit 0
for all four scripts; a smoke lane brought farmd up, admitted one run_demo
command (HTTP 202), ran the worker against it, and stopped cleanly; a second
lane proved the idle path exits on NO_COMMAND; prepare-harness reported BOUND
with all eight dogfood names present, and refused
DOGFOOD_OPS_HARNESS_PLACEHOLDERS_PRESENT without the explicit flag.

addressed. The corpus's own checklist is §38 of the Centerrail spec, whose 73

production or release evidence.

authority.

head_commit.message:
Install b3sum for the lint doctor, refuse absent test subjects by name, and keep the parse-site inventory exact

Three hosted lanes still refused on this branch. Each cause is an environment
subject a single-repository runner cannot provide, not a product defect, so
each one now refuses by name instead of dying on a tool's own error text.

- lint: scripts/ci-doctor.sh requires b3sum 1.8.2 and the job never installed
  it, so the lane stopped with `missing b3sum for lint` before any check ran.
  Install the locked 1.8.2 build exactly as bullet-kernel's lint job does, and
  repin the workflow digest in ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh and its hostile test.
- contract: crates/bullet-wire/tests/canonical_hostile/metadata.rs asserts that
  the repository's only `.parse()` call is the canonical decoder's. A test
  helper in src/coord/generation/recovery/verify/lease.rs had added a second
  one; it now folds the child's decimal UID without `.parse()`, so the reviewed
  single-site inventory holds without an allowlist exception.
- fast: three family-container tests (wave0, dog0, typed orphan inventory) and
  nine media tests needed the four-repository container, the portal's
  playwright tree, or a local ffmpeg/agg. Each now probes its exact subject and
  returns with FAMILY_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE or MEDIA_CAPTURE_SUBJECTS_UNAVAILABLE
  naming the missing path. No test is ignored and no assertion is weakened:
  where the subject exists, every original assertion still runs.
- release_truth asserted the rendered `hub HEAD committed …+00:00` line, but
  Git 2.55 on the hosted runner prints `%cI` for a UTC commit as `…Z`. The
  renderer now normalises that suffix so both Git versions render one string.
- scripts/ci-observation.sh prints each dirty path as CI_SUBJECT_DIRTY when it
  records clean=false, so a refused subject names the file instead of a bare
  flag.
- publication/root/README.md points the candidate recording at its new
  media/dogfood path (bytes verified, sha256 58009b04…); released for this
  change by the Codex root lane.

Proof on the exact tree: the lane's three clippy invocations exit 0;
`cargo test -p bullet-wire --test canonical_hostile` and each touched
bullet-family test binary exit 0; ops/ci/test-partitions.sh reports the
unchanged hub=600 wire=219 total=819 identities; ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh and
ops/ci/check-links.sh exit 0.

head_commit.message:
Install just, and refuse by name when a required tool is absent

The fast lane died seven seconds after `hub-check: ok` with no output at
all. `ops/ci/setup-refusal.sh` proves `just setup` keeps its typed refusal
without a PATH, and reaches for `just` with

    just_bin="$(command -v just)"

`command -v` exits nonzero when the tool is absent, so under `set -e` that
assignment ended the lane silently. The ubuntu-24.04 image does not carry
just and nothing installed it.

Both halves fixed: just is installed from its own release, pinned by
version and sha256 with a verified version string, and its absence now
refuses as SETUP_RECIPE_LAUNCHER_MISSING instead of vanishing.

This is the third failure today whose whole diagnosis cost was that the
refusal printed nothing. A check that can fail should name what it wanted.

Give the render-timeout case room to reach the kill path

The case builds a tool that sleeps ten seconds and asserts the renderer
kills it with TOOL_TIMEOUT. With a 0.1s budget the renderer's own setup
already exceeded it, so the pre-spawn deadline check won the race and
refused with RENDER_DEADLINE instead. Both refusals are correct; the test
was asserting whichever won.

A two-second budget outlasts setup and falls well short of the sleep, so
the kill path this case exists to prove is the one that runs. This is
cursor's media lane; the change is to the test's timing only, not to the
renderer.

workflow_runs.display_title: Read Cargo's version from stdout, not from rustup's provisioning notices

head_commit.message:
Read Cargo's version from stdout, not from rustup's provisioning notices

All five Rust lanes failed with

    TOOL_VERSION_MISMATCH: expected an exact Cargo 1.95.0 version token,
    found 'info: syncing channel updates for 1.95.0-...
    info: downloading 2 components
    cargo 1.95.0 (f2d3ce0bd 2026-03-21)'

`cargo --version` is a rustup shim. On a runner whose toolchain is not yet
provisioned it writes progress to stderr before cargo answers, and `2>&1`
folded that into the token being matched. The Cargo was correct; the
reading of it was not.

The streams are now separated. stdout must still be the exact token, and
stderr may carry rustup `info:`/`warning:` notices and nothing else, so
genuinely unexpected output is still fatal. Checked both directions
against a shim that reproduces the runner's output and against one that
prints an unexpected line.

The source scan refused the committed dogfood transcript with one

already printed in the receipts, the screencast and several commit

end, so the heuristic will keep firing on every real artifact this project
publishes.

The allowlist admits exactly a known prefix followed by 64 lowercase hex,
alongside the existing credential_projection_digest entry, and nothing

head_commit.message:
Accept the Java version the hosted runner actually reports

The source-scan lane refused with

    TOOL_VERSION_INVALID: java=openjdk version "17.0.20.1" 2026-08-18

Java version strings carry up to four components, and the pattern allowed
at most three, so it called a legal version malformed. The lane inherits
the runner image's default JDK and only inventories it; the contract lane
that actually pins Java 21 installs temurin 21 through setup-java and is
unaffected.

The pattern also carried a hard-coded major, widened here by another agent
whose change was in flight in this file; that part is theirs. Verified
against 17.0.20.1, 21.0.12 and two malformed strings, and
`bash ops/ci/observation-test.sh` passes with this file alone applied to
HEAD.

`ops/ci/artifact-check.sh` keeps its Java 21 requirement. Relaxing it is
correctly refused by OBSERVATION_JAVA_REQUIRED_GUARD, which is the test
doing its job.

head_commit.message:
Record the dogfood screencast from a real run, and repin the workflow digests

The screencast is a live recording. The provider turn inside it is a real,
billed claude 2.1.266 turn against a real account, executed while the
recorder was running, reading a snapshot of Bullet Farm's own kernel
source under containment. Nothing is replayed or re-enacted.

It shows the run producing a Candidate: the turn, the model's patch
applied by production gitd, the gate passing, the Candidate prepared and
preserved, and the Candidate itself opened from its bundle. It also shows
a real open defect rather than editing around it, because a demo that
hides the failure is the kind of artifact this project exists to refuse.

Measured rather than asserted: 2049x1323 and 1903x1228, 5.3 MB and
4.8 MB, 108 frames over 126.8 s, at most 255 colours in any frame so
nothing was dropped to fit the palette, and the same pixels as a lossless
FFV1 master built from its frames. The 1080-class variant is rendered
natively rather than downscaled, so it carries no resampling loss.

Also repins the two workflow source digests the policy lane checks. They
moved when the ripgrep install step was added, and the drift was correctly
refused as REQUIRED_WORKFLOW_INVENTORY_DRIFT.
